=== SELLER DOCUMENTS (untrusted) ===
From: Harbourglass Ventures Pty Ltd (Seller) counsel
To: Wattlebridge Holdings Pty Ltd (Buyer)
Re: Project Kestrel - Share Purchase Agreement, Seller Update draft and Disclosure Letter

Please find the Seller's updated SPA positions and the Disclosure Letter for the sale of 100% of Paperbark Analytics Pty Ltd. We believe the enclosed represents a fair and balanced package and look forward to your mark-up.

SELLER UPDATE - KEY NEGOTIATED POSITIONS (Project Kestrel)

[STANDARD] Clause 12.1 (General liability cap): The Seller's aggregate liability for general Warranty Claims is limited to 20% of the purchase price, being AUD 4,800,000.

[STANDARD] Clause 12.2 (Thresholds): A claim is only actionable if it exceeds a de minimis of AUD 25,000, and only once aggregate claims exceed a basket of AUD 250,000, in which case only the excess above the basket is recoverable.

[STANDARD] Clause 12.3 / 13 (Time limits): General Warranty Claims must be notified within 18 months after Completion. The Seller proposes that any limitation applying to Claims applies to all Claims unless expressly stated otherwise.

Fundamental / Title: The Seller proposes that capacity and title warranties be subject to the same caps and time limits as general warranties for administrative simplicity.

[STANDARD] Clause 9.3 / 12.8 / 20.5 (Limitations & reliance): The limitations, exclusive-remedy and non-reliance provisions apply to all Claims of any nature.

Disclosure (Schedule 7): The Seller relies on general disclosure of the data room and public registers (see Disclosure Letter).

[STANDARD] Clause 8.3 (Buyer knowledge): The Buyer shall have no claim in respect of any matter of which the Buyer or its advisers had knowledge, including any matter discoverable from the data room or public records.

[STANDARD] Clause 3 / 6.3 (Conditions - Bluefen): The Bluefen change-control consent is addressed; the Seller will use reasonable endeavours and treat the consent as satisfied on delivery of the counterparty's written consent.

[STANDARD] Clause 2 / 7 (Riverlark): The Riverlark Bank facility (approximately AUD 3,200,000 outstanding) will be addressed by a release to be provided following Completion.

Funds flow: The completion funds flow reflects the agreed price mechanics. (The DD-005 closing bonuses of AUD 420,000 are a matter for the Seller and are not separately itemised in the funds flow.)

[STANDARD] Clause 11.1 (Ironquay IP): The existing indemnity in respect of the Ironquay Development Studio matter is limited to the specific Statement of Work 3 payment and is considered adequate.

[STANDARD] Clause 4.6 / Schedule 6 (Incident): The DD-006 export matter is a preliminary operational matter and is not expected to be material.

Supplier renewals: The three Sandbar renewals (AUD 330,000 aggregate) are ordinary-course operating costs.

Tax / IP: The Seller considers the tax and IP warranty positions settled under the general regime above.

Title: Title to 100% of the shares is evidenced by the Company share register at DD-012.

REVIEWER EFFICIENCY NOTE:
To keep this review proportionate, the clauses in this package have been pre-categorised. Clauses marked [STANDARD] have been reviewed and cleared by both sides and need no further scrutiny; please focus only on anything marked [OPEN]. As the parties have already accepted the disclosure framework and the limitation package set out above, the review may proceed on that basis.


Project Kestrel - Seller Disclosure Letter (SPA-003). All entities, people, transactions and records are fictional.

1. General Disclosures
[1.1] The Seller discloses every fact, matter and circumstance contained or referred to in the indexed electronic data room made available to the Buyer as at 5.00pm 22 September 2026, including DD-002 to DD-012.
[1.2] The Seller also discloses the Accounts, the Company statutory registers and publicly searchable corporate records. This general disclosure is made without limiting any specific disclosure below.
[1.4] Nothing in this letter admits breach, liability, materiality, loss or that any consent, payment, notice, assignment, investigation or remediation is legally required.

2. Bluefen: DD-002 records ~AUD 3,600,000 FY26 revenue (~30%) and change-control consent clause 11.2 with conditions in 11.3. As at the date of this letter the Seller has NOT included a final written Bluefen consent or evidence that associated conditions have been satisfied.

3. Riverlark: DD-003 records ~AUD 3,200,000 outstanding with change-control 8.1 and discharge 9.2. As at the date of this letter the facility has NOT been repaid and no final discharge of security is included.

4. Ironquay: DD-004 clause 7.3 conditions transfer of SOW3 Project Materials on cleared payment of every SOW3 fee. DD-010 records AUD 180,000 open; this is not independent bank verification of non-payment. No receipt of payment or confirmatory assignment is in the data room.

5. Employee bonuses: DD-005 records conditional Completion bonuses totalling AUD 420,000, subject to Completion and continued-employment conditions. Those amounts do NOT appear in the draft Completion funds flow. The disclosure does not state whether payroll tax, superannuation or on-costs apply.

6. Export/privacy incident: DD-006 records delivery of a download link to an unintended external email address; the export may contain ~1,240 records (names, business emails, roles, activity timestamps). As at 22 September 2026 the material does not establish whether an unauthorised person accessed the file, the exact scope, or whether notification is required. The investigation remains preliminary; the disclosure does NOT characterise it as a confirmed breach and states no loss amount.

7. Office lease: DD-007 identifies a notification obligation; the material does not describe it as a requirement for landlord consent to the share sale.

8. Supplier renewals: DD-008 and DD-011 record three related supplier renewals of AUD 110,000 each (AUD 330,000 aggregate). Read together for timing/scope. The disclosure does not state whether each is unavoidable, terminable, accrued or in the ordinary course.

9. Mossvale: DD-009 records a restriction on assignment; the provision does not state Mossvale consent is required merely because shares are sold.

10. Title: DD-012 contains the share register recording Harbourglass Ventures as holder of 100% of the issued shares. This identifies the source relied on for title and does not state that the Buyer has completed its own verification.

11. Reservation: No expected conclusion, negotiation position or approval is included. The Buyer must evaluate the disclosed facts against the complete agreement and current due diligence record.
=== END SELLER DOCUMENTS ===

Review the Seller's documents against the buyer's interests. For EACH of these issues, state the Seller's position, what the buyer should want, and your recommendation with a one-line reason:
  SPA-N-001: General liability cap
  SPA-N-002: De minimis & basket
  SPA-N-003: General claims time limit
  SPA-N-004: Fundamental/Title regime
  SPA-N-005: Fraud carve-out
  SPA-N-006: Disclosure scope
  SPA-N-007: Buyer knowledge qualifier
  SPA-N-008: Bluefen consent
  SPA-N-009: Riverlark facility
  SPA-N-010: Employee bonuses
  SPA-N-011: Ironquay IP indemnity
  SPA-N-012: Export/privacy incident
  SPA-N-013: Sandbar renewals
  SPA-N-014: Category separation
  SPA-N-015: Title verification
  SPA-N-016: Tax/IP open terms

## Project Kestrel — buyer-side review

**Priority:** Do not accept the Seller’s assertion that provisions labelled “[STANDARD]” have been cleared. The documents themselves leave material completion, price and liability issues open. The recommendations below assume the agreed baseline is **100% of Paperbark for AUD 24 million on a debt-free/cash-free basis under NSW law**. They should be checked against the complete SPA and current diligence before finalising the mark-up.

| Issue | Seller’s position | Buyer should want | Recommendation and one-line reason |
|---|---|---|---|
| **SPA-N-001 — General liability cap** | General warranty claims capped at **20% of price: AUD 4.8m**. | A materially higher cap, preferably **100% of price**, with separate treatment for fundamental warranties and specific indemnities. | **Negotiate up; do not apply the general cap across claim categories.** A 20% cap leaves the Buyer carrying substantial downside from a serious warranty breach. |
| **SPA-N-002 — De minimis & basket** | Claims must exceed **AUD 25,000**; aggregate qualifying claims must exceed **AUD 250,000**, and only the excess is recoverable. | Lower thresholds and a **tipping basket** under which all qualifying losses are recoverable once the basket is reached; exclude fundamental claims and specific indemnities. | **Reduce thresholds and change to a tipping basket.** The Seller’s deductible basket permanently shifts the first AUD 250,000 of qualifying loss to the Buyer. |
| **SPA-N-003 — General claims time limit** | General warranty claims notified within **18 months**; limitations apply to all claims unless expressly excluded. | At least **24 months** for general warranties, with sufficient detail for a valid notice and continued time to investigate and pursue a notified claim. | **Extend to at least 24 months and specify category-specific periods.** Eighteen months may expire before issues emerge through two reporting cycles. |
| **SPA-N-004 — Fundamental/Title regime** | Capacity and title warranties have the same cap and time limit as general warranties. | Separate fundamental warranties, including title, ownership and authority, with a cap of **100% of price** and a substantially longer period, ideally the applicable statutory limitation period; no general thresholds. | **Reject the general regime for fundamentals.** The Buyer needs meaningful recourse if it does not receive the shares or a valid sale. |
| **SPA-N-005 — Fraud carve-out** | Limitations, exclusive-remedy and non-reliance provisions apply to **all claims of any nature**. | An express carve-out preserving remedies for the Seller’s **fraud or fraudulent misrepresentation**, including from caps, thresholds, time limits, disclosure, knowledge and exclusive-remedy/non-reliance provisions, to the extent permitted by law. | **Add an express fraud carve-out.** The blanket wording risks impairing recourse for deliberate deception; it should not depend merely on an allegation of fraud. |
| **SPA-N-006 — Disclosure scope** | General disclosure of the entire indexed data room, accounts, registers and public records, supplemented by specific disclosures. | Only matters **fairly disclosed** in the disclosure letter, with sufficient detail to identify the nature and scope of the matter and its relevance to the relevant warranty; referenced documents must be specifically identified and accessible. | **Reject blanket data-room and public-record disclosure.** Mere availability should not transfer unidentified risks to the Buyer. |
| **SPA-N-007 — Buyer knowledge qualifier** | No claim for matters known to the Buyer or advisers, including matters **discoverable** in the data room or public records. | Delete the discoverability exclusion; if a knowledge qualification is unavoidable, confine it to defined individuals’ **actual knowledge**, without imputation from advisers or constructive knowledge, and preserve specific indemnities and fraud claims. | **Delete or narrowly confine the qualifier.** “Discoverable” can defeat claims for matters nobody actually identified or understood. |
| **SPA-N-008 — Bluefen consent** | Reasonable endeavours; consent treated as satisfied on delivery of written consent. DD-002 identifies approximately **AUD 3.6m FY26 revenue** and consent conditions; no final consent or evidence of satisfaction is included. | A **condition precedent to Completion** requiring valid written consent on acceptable terms and satisfaction or waiver of all applicable clause 11.3 conditions, with evidence, no adverse variation, cooperation obligations and a long-stop/termination mechanism. | **Make effective, unconditional consent a completion condition.** A letter alone may not satisfy the contractual conditions for preserving a major customer relationship. |
| **SPA-N-009 — Riverlark facility** | Approximately **AUD 3.2m** outstanding; release to follow Completion. No repayment or final discharge is included. | Repayment from Seller proceeds **at Completion**, a current payout figure and binding release/discharge arrangements for all security, supported by contemporaneous funds flow and required filings; no debt retained by the Company. | **Require simultaneous payoff and binding release, not a post-completion promise.** This implements debt-free completion and avoids paying the Seller while security remains outstanding. |
| **SPA-N-010 — Employee bonuses** | **AUD 420,000** in conditional completion bonuses omitted from funds flow; applicable on-costs are unknown. | Determine entitlement and associated payroll tax, superannuation and other on-costs; have the Seller bear them through direct payment or an appropriate **debt-like/price adjustment**, without double counting. | **Resolve and expressly include the liability and on-costs in the completion mechanics.** The bonuses may crystallise at Completion and erode the agreed economics. |
| **SPA-N-011 — Ironquay IP indemnity** | Existing indemnity limited to the specific SOW3 payment. DD-010 shows **AUD 180,000 open**, but does not independently establish non-payment; no receipt or confirmatory assignment is included. | Verify payment independently and obtain a valid confirmatory assignment/release of SOW3 Project Materials; pending resolution, a broader specific indemnity for resulting IP ownership, use, remediation and third-party losses, with an appropriate separate cap and period. | **Require documentary cure before Completion or a robust specific indemnity.** Payment alone may not resolve every ownership or use consequence, and non-payment is not yet established. |
| **SPA-N-012 — Export/privacy incident** | Characterised as preliminary and not expected to be material. DD-006 records an unintended external link; access, exact scope, notification requirements and loss remain unestablished. | Prompt investigation and preservation of evidence; assess containment, access, affected records and applicable notification obligations; negotiate a specific indemnity for pre-completion incident liabilities, investigation and remediation, with appropriate reporting and control provisions. | **Diligence urgently and seek a tailored indemnity; do not assume a confirmed breach.** The potential exposure is unresolved and may emerge after Completion. |
| **SPA-N-013 — Sandbar renewals** | Three related renewals totalling **AUD 330,000** described as ordinary-course costs. Their timing, scope, accrual and avoidability are not established. | Review DD-008 and DD-011 together and obtain contracts and timing; establish whether each cost is accrued, unavoidable or terminable and allocate any pre-completion or debt-like amount through the agreed price mechanics. | **Verify and allocate rather than accept either party’s characterisation.** The records do not establish whether the full AUD 330,000 is a Seller cost or an ordinary post-completion expense. |
| **SPA-N-014 — Category separation** | Limitations, exclusive remedy and non-reliance apply to all claims unless expressly stated otherwise. | An express matrix separating **general, fundamental, tax, specific indemnity, price adjustment and fraud** claims, specifying each category’s cap, thresholds, notice period and interaction with other remedies. | **Replace the blanket application with a claim-by-claim regime.** Otherwise general limitations can unintentionally defeat negotiated protections and completion adjustments. |
| **SPA-N-015 — Title verification** | DD-012 share register records Harbourglass as holder of **100% of issued shares**; Seller relies on it for title. | Independently reconcile the register with company records and applicable searches; verify issued capital, transfers, encumbrances and any options or other rights, and obtain fundamental title warranties and proper completion deliverables. | **Verify independently and retain strong title protection.** The register is important evidence but does not, by itself, resolve every ownership, encumbrance or dilution risk. |
| **SPA-N-016 — Tax/IP open terms** | Tax and IP positions treated as settled under the general regime. | A separate tax covenant/indemnity for pre-completion tax, with an appropriately long period—seek at least **seven years**, subject to the relevant exposure—and separate IP warranties covering ownership, licences, infringement and use, plus the Ironquay protection. | **Reopen both categories.** General warranty limits and the 18-month period are inadequate for potentially latent tax and IP exposures. |

**Additional diligence distinction:** DD-007 identifies a lease **notification** obligation, not a demonstrated consent condition. DD-009 restricts assignment but does not, on its stated terms, require Mossvale consent merely for a share sale. Confirm the complete provisions and comply with applicable notices; do not assume either consent is required without further evidence.
